## Summary

`theme.favicon_url` is a documented auth-config key. It is validated, resolved,
and passed into the template context — and then nothing renders it. The hosted
`/auth`, `/register` and `/passkey` pages always serve the deployment's own
`/favicon/*` files, so a white-label tenant that sets `favicon_url` sees the
host's favicon in the browser tab, not theirs.

## Evidence

The value survives all the way to the template context:

- `mojo/apps/account/services/auth_config.py:53` — `"favicon_url": ""` in `DEFAULT_AUTH_CONFIG`
- `mojo/apps/account/rest/bouncer/views.py:323` — `'favicon_url': theme.favicon_url or '',` in `_auth_context()`

Then `mojo/apps/account/templates/account/auth_base.html:7-11` hardcodes it away:

```html
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/favicon/apple-touch-icon.png">
<link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="32x32" href="/favicon/favicon-32x32.png">
<link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="16x16" href="/favicon/favicon-16x16.png">
<link rel="manifest" href="/favicon/site.webmanifest">
<link rel="shortcut icon" href="/favicon/favicon.ico">
```

`grep -rn favicon_url mojo/apps/account/templates/` returns **nothing** — no
template reads the context key. Every other `theme.*` key in that context dict
is rendered somewhere; this is the only orphan.

It is documented as working in both tracks, which is what makes it a bug rather
than a missing feature:

- `docs/django_developer/account/auth_config.md:40` — the schema table lists it
- `docs/django_developer/account/auth_config.md:264` — the migration table maps the retired `AUTH_FAVICON_URL` onto it, so deployments were told to move to a key that does nothing
- `docs/web_developer/account/auth_config.md:45` — appears in the public example config

## Impact

Cosmetic but squarely against the point of the bouncer white-label work: the
auth page is the one surface a tenant's users see before they are signed in,
and the tab icon is wrong on it. Silent — no warning, no validation error; the
setting simply has no effect.

## Suggested fix

Render it in `auth_base.html`, falling back to the current hardcoded set so no
existing deployment changes:

```html
{% if favicon_url %}
<link rel="icon" href="{{ favicon_url }}">
{% else %}
  ... existing five /favicon/* links ...
{% endif %}
```

Worth deciding whether `favicon_url` should also be constrained to `https://`
(or a `data:` URI) the way `custom_css_url` is via `_validate_https_url` —
`logo_url` and `hero_image_url` are currently unconstrained too, so following
their precedent and leaving it unvalidated is defensible.

## How it surfaced

Found while theming maestro's hosted auth pages (maestro repo,
`config/settings/defaults/auth_pages.py`). We set `favicon_url` to the maestro
mark, saw no change in the tab, and traced it to the template. Maestro keeps
the setting in place for when this lands and documents the gap in
`docs/django_developer/maestro/Auth.md`.

## Verification

Set `AUTH_CONFIG.theme.favicon_url` to any reachable image, load `/auth`, and
check the `<link rel="icon">` in the rendered head — today it is unchanged.
Framework suite: `tests/test_auth_config/`.

## Plan

### Objective

When `theme.favicon_url` is non-empty it renders as the only favicon
declaration on every hosted auth page, so a white-label tenant's browser tab
shows their icon. When it is empty — every existing deployment — the rendered
HTML is byte-identical to today.

### Implementation steps

**1. `mojo/apps/account/templates/account/auth_base.html`** — replace lines
7-11 (the five hardcoded `/favicon/*` links) with:

```html
    {% if favicon_url %}
    <link rel="icon" href="{{ favicon_url }}">
    {% else %}
    <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/favicon/apple-touch-icon.png">
    <link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="32x32" href="/favicon/favicon-32x32.png">
    <link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="16x16" href="/favicon/favicon-16x16.png">
    <link rel="manifest" href="/favicon/site.webmanifest">
    <link rel="shortcut icon" href="/favicon/favicon.ico">
    {% endif %}
```

This is the entire code change. Do **not** add `|safe` (it would reopen an
attribute-breakout vector) and do **not** add a `type=` attribute (a wrong type
breaks the icon; browsers sniff). No view, service, or Python change is needed:
`favicon_url` already reaches the context of all four templates that extend
`auth_base.html`, via `_auth_context()` (`views.py:258`), whose three call
sites are `views.py:247` (passkey), `:358` (login/register) and `:492`
(contact).

**2. `tests/test_auth_config/auth_config.py`** — add the render helper and
three tests (see Testing plan).

**3. `docs/django_developer/account/auth_config.md:40`** — the `favicon_url`
Description cell currently reads `Favicon URL`. Rewrite it to state the
contract: favicon URL or path; when set it is the only icon declared on the
hosted auth pages, and the deployment's default `/favicon/*` links and web
manifest are suppressed.

**4. `docs/django_developer/account/auth_pages.md:97-98`** — the existing
sentence ("Set `theme.favicon_url` in `AUTH_CONFIG` to your favicon path — the
template includes `<link rel="icon" href="...">` when this key is non-empty")
becomes true as written once step 1 lands and needs no correction. Append one
clause noting that the default `/favicon/*` links and the web manifest are
suppressed when it is set.

**5. `docs/web_developer/account/auth_config.md`** — add one sentence to the
per-group branding section noting that the browser tab icon follows the group's
`theme.favicon_url`. The `GET /api/auth/config` response shape is unchanged.

**6. `CHANGELOG.md`** — insert a new `## Unreleased` block at the very top (the
current top block, `## v1.2.59 - July 29, 2026`, is released; the repo's
convention is a rolling `## Unreleased` block that the release commit
re-headers — see `6cb68d3b` → `76332c8b`) with a `**fix (account)** — ` entry
in the house style.

### Design decisions

**Suppress all five defaults rather than appending.** Appending
`<link rel="icon">` alongside the deployment's `sizes="16x16"`/`sizes="32x32"`
PNGs leaves icon selection to browser heuristics — Chrome scores candidates by
declared size, and an un-`sizes`'d link frequently loses to a sized one. The
`{% if %}/{% else %}` gives the browser exactly one candidate, so the outcome is
deterministic. The manifest is suppressed deliberately: `site.webmanifest` also
declares icons that can win over the `<link>`, and a host-branded manifest is
the wrong metadata to serve a tenant. Verified there is no in-repo coupling to
that manifest link — no `theme-color` meta and no service-worker registration
anywhere in `mojo/`, and `site.webmanifest` is referenced from exactly one line
in the codebase. Cost: a deployment that opts into `favicon_url` loses
`theme-color`/PWA install metadata and the iOS home-screen icon **on the auth
pages only**. That is an opt-in trade, documented in step 3, not a silent one.

**Do not add `_validate_https_url` to `favicon_url`.** Settled by the docs, not
by taste: `docs/django_developer/account/auth_pages.md:97` instructs
deployments to set it to "your favicon **path**", and `auth_config.md:264` maps
the retired `AUTH_FAVICON_URL` onto it. An https-only validator would reject
the documented relative-path usage and break the advertised migration path at
`Group` save time. It also matches precedent: `_validate_https_url` is applied
to exactly one key (`custom_css_url`, `auth_config.py:245-246`), because a
stylesheet can restyle the page and exfiltrate; `logo_url` and `hero_image_url`
are both unconstrained, and an icon is in that class.

**Rely on Django autoescaping rather than a sanitizer.** Autoescape is on (the
`DjangoTemplates` backend is configured with no `autoescape` option) and
`_auth_context` returns plain `str`, never a `SafeString`; the only `|safe` in
this template is `custom_css` at line 14. `{{ favicon_url }}` inside an
attribute is therefore escaped (`"` → `&quot;`, `<` → `&lt;`, `&` → `&amp;`),
which closes attribute breakout. `&amp;` in an href is entity-decoded by the
browser back to `&`, so query strings survive intact — which is exactly why
`|safe` must not be used here.

**Test with an in-process render, not an HTTP GET.** `/auth` is bouncer-gated
and serves the challenge page to a cold client, so `opts.client.get('/auth')`
would assert against the wrong template. `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py:41-53`
already establishes the `RequestFactory` + `_auth_context` + `render()` pattern
for exactly this reason; follow it.

### Edge cases and error handling

- **Empty / unset** — `_auth_context` already normalizes with
  `theme.favicon_url or ''`, so `""` and `None` are both falsy and take the
  `{% else %}` branch. No existing deployment changes. Pinned by test 2.
- **`javascript:` URL** — not an XSS vector. An icon `href` is fetched as a
  subresource, never navigated; the fetch fails and the browser falls back.
  Residual risk: a missing icon.
- **`"`- or tag-containing value** — neutralized by autoescaping. This is the
  one genuinely dangerous vector and it is closed, conditional on no `|safe`;
  test 3 pins that.
- **`http://` URL on an https page** — the browser blocks the mixed-content
  subresource and the tab falls back to the default icon. Cosmetic and
  self-inflicted; the alternative (an https validator) breaks the documented
  relative-path usage. Not handled.
- **Whitespace-only value** — truthy, renders `href="   "`, resolves to the
  current page and fails to decode as an image. Identical to `logo_url`'s
  behavior today; deliberately not stripped, for consistency.
- **Threat model** — `theme.favicon_url` is written by the deployment's
  `AUTH_CONFIG` setting or through `group.metadata["auth_config"]`, which
  requires `manage_groups`. Admin-level config, not end-user input. The
  third-party-request/IP-leak property is identical to `logo_url` and
  `hero_image_url` today, so no new exposure class.
- **Out of scope** — `bouncer_challenge.html`, which most first-time visitors
  see *before* the login page, declares no favicon links at all and does not
  receive `_auth_context` (`_serve_challenge` builds its own context at
  `views.py:401`). Its tab icon stays the browser's `/favicon.ico` probe. Not
  expanded here.

### Testing plan

File: **`tests/test_auth_config/auth_config.py`** — its setup already creates
`opts.group` at `AC_GROUP_UUID`, and `_reset_metadata(*groups)` exists at line
57. `test_resolve_group_override` (lines 81-99) proves a `group.metadata`
mutation is visible to `resolve_auth_config` in-process with no caching in the
way, which is what makes this approach work.

Add a module-level helper modeled on `tests/test_auth/bouncer_forms.py:41-53`:

```python
FAVICON_URL = 'https://cdn.example.com/tenant-favicon.png'
HOSTED_TEMPLATES = ('account/login.html', 'account/register.html',
                    'account/passkey_enroll.html', 'account/contact.html')


def _render_auth_page(template_name, group=None):
    from django.test import RequestFactory
    from django.shortcuts import render
    from mojo.apps.account.rest.bouncer.views import _auth_context
    factory = RequestFactory()
    request = factory.get('/auth')
    ctx = _auth_context(request, group=group)
    ctx['page_mode'] = 'login'
    ctx['page_title'] = 'Sign In'
    return render(request, template_name, ctx).content.decode('utf-8')
```

Set the favicon via `opts.group.metadata` inside
`try/finally: _reset_metadata(opts.group)` — the pattern already used at lines
84-99 and 231-246.

1. **`test_favicon_url_renders_on_hosted_pages`** — group sets
   `theme.favicon_url = FAVICON_URL`; loop `HOSTED_TEMPLATES`. Per template
   assert (a) `f'<link rel="icon" href="{FAVICON_URL}">'` is in the HTML and
   (b) `'/favicon/'` is **not**. **Fails on old code on both halves** — the
   tenant link is absent (no template reads the key today) and all five
   `/favicon/*` links are present. Passes only with the fix. The positive
   assertion is what keeps the test non-vacuous: a degraded render would not
   contain the tenant link either.
2. **`test_favicon_url_unset_keeps_deployment_icons`** — render with
   `group=None`; assert all five default paths are present and
   `'<link rel="icon" href="">'` is absent. Passes before and after — the
   no-regression guard proving the `{% else %}` branch is untouched.
3. **`test_favicon_url_is_html_escaped`** — set `favicon_url` to
   `'https://cdn.example.com/i.png"><script>alert(1)</script>'`; render
   `account/login.html`; assert `'<script>alert(1)</script>'` is **not** in the
   HTML and `'&quot;'` **is**. Guards against a future `|safe`.

Every assert carries a descriptive failure message (`assert_true` / `assert_eq`
from `testit.helpers`, already imported in the file). No `mock.patch`, no
`override_settings` — the render is in-process, so neither is needed and
neither would reach `opts.client`'s separate server anyway.

Baseline (`.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`) — captured before any edit, green:
**2984 tests, 2928 passed, 0 failed, 56 skipped** (`--agent`, no `--full`; the
329 opt-in tests in `test_incident` and `test_security` were not run). Every
failure after this change is therefore attributable to it.

Prove the regression first: run test 1 **before** applying step 1 and confirm
it fails on both assertions; then apply and confirm green.

Run: `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_auth_config.auth_config`, then the default
suite `bin/run_tests --agent` compared against the baseline. Not `--full`.

### Schema impact

None. No model, field, table, or migration is touched. `bin/create_testproject`
does not need to run.

### Contract changes

- **A deployment that does not set `theme.favicon_url` sees no change at all.**
  The `{% else %}` branch is byte-identical to the current lines 7-11, and
  `_auth_context` already normalizes empty/`None` to `''`, which is falsy.
  Pinned by test 2.
- **A deployment that does set it** gets a single
  `<link rel="icon" href="...">` and loses the five default `/favicon/*` links —
  including `site.webmanifest`, so PWA install metadata, `theme-color` and the
  iOS home-screen icon are no longer declared on the auth pages for that
  tenant. Intended contract; documented.
- Affects **four** pages, not the three the Summary names: `/auth`
  (`login.html`), `/register` (`register.html`), `/passkey`
  (`passkey_enroll.html`) and `/contact` (`contact.html`) — all four extend
  `auth_base.html` and all four receive `favicon_url`.
- No endpoint, URL, view signature, or serialization shape changes.
  `GET /api/auth/config` already returns `theme.favicon_url` and is unaffected.
  `validate_auth_config` is unchanged — no config that validates today starts
  failing.

### Premise check

Every factual claim in the workspec is **true as written**, verified line by
line: `auth_config.py:53`, `views.py:323`, `auth_base.html:7-11` (the five
links, exactly as quoted), and no template referencing `favicon_url`. The "only
orphan" claim holds — every other theme-derived context key resolves to at
least one template; `favicon_url` alone resolves to zero. No child template
overrides a head block (there is no head block; children define only
`page_title`, `title`, `subtitle_block`, `content`, `switcher`, `extra_css`,
`page_script`), so the favicon markup exists in exactly one place, and there is
exactly one `auth_base.html` on the template search path.

Four things the workspec omits:

1. **A fourth affected page.** The Summary covers "`/auth`, `/register` and
   `/passkey`". `/contact` (`contact.html`) also extends `auth_base.html` and is
   rendered by `_serve_contact` from the same `_auth_context`, so it is affected
   identically. The fix covers it automatically; the test loop covers it
   explicitly.
2. **A fourth doc reference, and the strongest one.**
   `docs/django_developer/account/auth_pages.md:97-98` states outright that
   "the template includes `<link rel="icon" href="...">` when this key is
   non-empty" — it specifies the exact markup, so it pins the implementation
   rather than merely describing the feature, and needs no correction once the
   fix lands.
3. **The open validation question is already settled — against validating.**
   The workspec calls leaving `favicon_url` unvalidated "defensible". It is
   stronger than that: the same `auth_pages.md:97` line tells deployments to
   set it to a *path*, so adding `_validate_https_url` would make documented
   usage fail validation at `Group` save time and break the advertised
   `AUTH_FAVICON_URL` migration.
4. **The challenge page is a separate, untouched gap.**
   `bouncer_challenge.html` — which most first-time human visitors see *before*
   the login page — declares no favicon links at all and does not receive
   `_auth_context`. Fixing `auth_base.html` does not affect it. Out of scope;
   worth a follow-up item.

### Challenge

The independent red-team sub-agent died three times on API 529s
(server-side overload). The challenge was therefore run **in-session against
the repo** rather than by a fresh-context agent — a deviation from the scoping
protocol, recorded here rather than glossed. Every objection below was verified
by reading the code, not reasoned about abstractly.

- **"The `bouncer_forms.py:41-53` render helper is a hallucination."**
  `rebutted` — read it; lines 41-53 are exactly that helper, and
  `_auth_context(request, group=None)` is the real signature at `views.py:258`.
- **"`'/favicon/' not in html` will fail even with a correct fix, because
  `/favicon/` appears elsewhere."** `rebutted` — `grep -rn favicon --include="*.html"`
  across the whole repo returns only `auth_base.html:7-11`. The negative
  assertion is safe.
- **"Suppressing `site.webmanifest` breaks a paired `theme-color` meta or a
  service worker."** `rebutted` — neither exists anywhere in `mojo/`. The
  manifest link has no in-repo dependents. The PWA/`theme-color` loss is real
  but is browser-side metadata only, opt-in, and now documented.
- **"`## Unreleased` is not this repo's CHANGELOG convention — the top block is
  a released version."** `rebutted` with evidence: commit `6cb68d3b` added
  `## Unreleased`, and release commit `76332c8b` re-headered it to
  `## v1.2.59 - July 29, 2026`. A rolling `## Unreleased` block is exactly the
  convention.
- **"Test 1 could be vacuous — a broken in-process render would satisfy
  `'/favicon/' not in html` trivially."** `amended` — the risk is real for the
  negative half alone. The plan pairs it with a positive assertion on the
  tenant link, which a degraded render cannot satisfy, and test 2 independently
  pins the `{% else %}` branch. Noted explicitly in the Testing plan.
- **"The plan tests three templates but four extend `auth_base.html`."**
  `amended` — `HOSTED_TEMPLATES` now includes `account/contact.html`.
- **Surviving objection, escalated to the user rather than rebutted:**
  suppressing all five default links goes beyond what
  `auth_pages.md:97-98` promises — it says the template *includes*
  `<link rel="icon">` when the key is set, not that it *replaces* the defaults.
  Suppression is the better behavior (deterministic icon selection) and there is
  no in-repo coupling, but it is a product decision the user may reverse, so it
  was raised at the approval gate.
